function.mechanism: Acts as a pressurized gas to dispense and aerate products; may also be used as headspace gas in packaging applications.
common_food_categories: Packaged foods using gas headspace systems

adi.basis: No completed EFSA re-evaluation opinion with a numeric ADI was identified for E942; EFSA lists E942 among remaining additives in the re-evaluation programme.

efsa.key_finding: E942 is among remaining EU-permitted additives for which EFSA requested additional technical data; no finalized EFSA re-evaluation conclusion for E942 was identified in the accessed sources.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA database lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED.

concerns.summary: Human misuse and animal studies indicate neurologic injury potential at sustained/high inhalation exposure, with vitamin B12 functional inhibition and downstream neurologic effects.
Animal-data systematic review supports reproductive/developmental toxicity concern at high occupational inhalation exposures and proposes an occupational exposure limit.

no_concern_confirmed: FDA affirms nitrous oxide as GRAS direct human food ingredient under GMP in 21 CFR 184.1545.
JECFA lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED and accepted use as food propellant (historical conclusion).

adi_exceedance.notes: Numeric ADI exceedance cannot be computed because JECFA ADI is NOT SPECIFIED and no numeric EFSA ADI from a completed E942 re-evaluation was identified.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory data support low concern for intended food-additive use (FDA GRAS; JECFA ADI not specified), but robust evidence of harm exists at high inhalation exposure (misuse/occupational contexts). EFSA re-evaluation for E942 appears incomplete in the accessed sources, so a fully risk_free classification is not justified.
key_factors: FDA GRAS status with GMP conditions (21 CFR 184.1545)
JECFA ADI NOT SPECIFIED and historical acceptance of propellant use
EFSA still treating E942 as part of remaining additives under re-evaluation
Recent epidemiological and mechanistic evidence of harm at high non-dietary inhalation exposure
